newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Steel sets 1997/98 pretax target.
newsitem.headline: China Steel sets 1997/98 pretax target.

text.p: Taiwan's top steel maker, China Steel Corp, said its board on Tuesday set a 1997/1998 (July/June) pretax profit target of T$20.4 billion, up from 1996/1997 target of T$17 billion.
The board set a 1997/98 sales target of T$96.168 billion, China Steel said in a statement. It did not set a sales target for 1996/97.
"Due to the completion of our expansion and recent international steel price hikes, we expect both our sales and profits to rise sharply in 1997/98," the statement said.
"Our 1997/1998 earnings per share will reach T$2.25, a record high for the company," it said.
It did not give a 1996/1997 comparison figure.
China Steel completed a new T$57.4 billion plant and began operations in November 1996.
The expansion has increased the firm's annual steel production capacity to 8.05 million tonnes from 5.65 million.
China Steel, previously state-run, was privatised in April 1995.
